fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's field guidelines say a turf base should be compacted thoroughly to prevent differential settlement, with special attention to compacting the backfill of any utility trench that crosses the turf area.
quote: The base materials should be thoroughly compacted to prevent differential settlement across the field area. Minimum compaction levels typically should not be less than 95% density as measured by a standard proctor test. Special attention should be given to backfill compaction of any utility trenches that cross the field area. Care should also be taken not to over compact, which could affect drainage.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Suggested Guidelines for the Essential Elements of Synthetic Turf Systems (revised Nov. 2011), 4.2.3
notes: Written for sports fields; the page uses it only for the trench-backfill point. Read from the PDF (pdftotext) on 2026-09-25.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council says irregularities in the base show through in the finished turf, holds a sports-field base to within 1/4 inch under a 10-foot straightedge, and says hollows and depressions found while compacting should be filled and re-compacted.
quote: Irregularities in the surface of the base materials are typically reflected in the finished field surface. Therefore, it is important to install the base materials to controlled tolerances. … The local deviation of the finished surface of the base stone should not exceed ¼ in. in any direction when measured beneath a 10-foot long straight edge (6mm in 3m). Hollows and depressions, which may have developed during the process of compacting the base, should be filled with acceptable material and re-compacted.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Suggested Guidelines for the Essential Elements of Synthetic Turf Systems (revised Nov. 2011), 5.3.4
notes: A sports-field tolerance, not a residential one; the page labels it that way.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's base guidelines say subgrade preparation removes topsoil, organic matter, stumps and roots, large stones and soil that does not meet compaction standards, and that cavities are filled with suitable fill compacted in 6-inch lifts.
quote: Removal of all topsoil, organic matter, minerals such as mica, stumps and roots, large stones, foreign matter, and soil that does not meet compaction standards or is “plastic”. … Repair of surface cavities using suitable fill either excavated from the site, or brought to the site at additional cost. Fill must be compacted in 6” lifts as the fill moves upward.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Guidelines for Base Systems (2017), 5.1.1 Sub-Grade Preparation
notes: Sports-field guidance. The organic-soil sentences from the same PDF are can-you-put-artificial-turf-over-grass-or-dirt.stc-organic-soils.

fact: The Colorado Geological Survey says expansive clay that was wet and then dries out shrinks and loses volume, and that the same soil can swell and shrink any number of times.
quote: The opposite effect, called shrinkage, may occur if a previously wet expansive clay is dried. Although no large positive pressures are exerted, shrinkage will cause a volume decrease of the soil mass. These processes of expansion and shrinkage may occur any number of times for a single soil mass.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey, Expansive Soil & Rock
notes: The page applies this to a lawn that was watered for years and then stops being watered once it is turf; that application is the page's inference, hedged with "can".

fact: A Colorado Geological Survey homeowner publication says uneven movement of clay soils usually comes from uneven changes in soil moisture, from drainage patterns, local watering, evaporation and trees and shrubs drawing water out of the soil.
quote: Differential heave, rather than total movement, is generally responsible for major structural damage. Differential movements are usually caused by non-uniform changes in soil moisture and irregularities in the thickness and composition of the foundation clay strata. Variations in soil moisture may result from edge effects of wetting or drying on a covered area, which may involve seasonal or cyclic (long time) weather changes, drainage patterns, local watering, or drying of soils from evaporation and where shrubs and trees remove soil moisture by transpiration.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-11, Home Construction on Shrinking and Swelling Soils (Holtz and Hart, Oct. 1978)
notes: Scanned 1978 publication, still distributed by CGS. The OCR joins "movementsare"; the quote restores the space. The introduction names an out-of-territory metro example; never quote that passage.

fact: The same Colorado Geological Survey publication says uncorrected settlement of soil near a foundation creates ponding of rain, snowmelt and irrigation water, and that downspouts should carry roof runoff at least 10 feet from the house.
quote: All downspouts and splash blocks should be placed so that roof runoff will be carried at least 10 feet from the building. … The most critical aspect of landscaping is the continual maintenance of properly designed slopes. Flattening slopes, or not correcting settlement of the soil near foundations, will create ponding of rain, snowmelt and irrigation water.
source_label: Colorado Geological Survey SP-11, Home Construction on Shrinking and Swelling Soils (Holtz and Hart, Oct. 1978)

fact: FusionTurf, a turf maker, repairs a turf base by folding the turf back, marking the soft, low or ponding area, digging out loose base down to firm support, rebuilding in 1- to 2-inch lifts of clean, lightly dampened aggregate compacted with 2 to 4 overlapping passes each, hand-tamping edges, then relaying the turf, resetting seams and reapplying infill.
quote: Fold back the turf and secure it to protect edges and backing. Identify soft, low, or ponding areas and mark the boundaries. … Excavate loose or contaminated base until you reach firm support. … Add clean aggregate in 1 to 2 inch lifts. Mist lightly so the mix is damp, not muddy. Compact each lift with 2 to 4 overlapping passes in a cross pattern until it feels solid underfoot. … Hand tamp edges, borders, and tight corners the plate cannot reach. … Relay turf, reset seams, brush fibers upright, and reapply infill as needed.
source_label: FusionTurf, Can I use a plate compactor when repairing my turf base?
notes: Undated manufacturer answer page; read in full with curl on 2026-09-25.

fact: FusionTurf calls a landscape turf base within about 1/2 inch over 10 feet acceptable, aims for about 1/4 inch over 10 feet on performance areas, and checks the fall with a level, laser or taut string line.
quote: Use a level, laser, or taut string line to confirm the 1 to 2 percent fall. … On performance areas, aim for flatness within about 1/4 inch over 10 feet. For general landscapes, within about 1/2 inch over 10 feet is acceptable.
source_label: FusionTurf, Can I use a plate compactor when repairing my turf base?

fact: FusionTurf says to stop and fix the cause before rebuilding a turf base: dry or stabilize a subgrade that pumps water, dig out organic soil or clay pockets, give trapped water a slope or drain line, and never rebuild with round rock, pea gravel, topsoil or clay.
quote: If the subgrade pumps or smears, let it dry or stabilize with geotextile and additional aggregate. If organic soil or clay pockets are present, remove and replace with compactable aggregate. If water is trapped, create a path with slope or a drain line before rebuilding. … Avoid round rock, pea gravel, topsoil, or clay. They do not compact into a stable, drainable layer for turf.
source_label: FusionTurf, Can I use a plate compactor when repairing my turf base?

fact: CSU Extension says voles build surface runways and underground tunnels, lists spongy soil from burrowing among the signs, and says most of their damage happens in winter when they travel under snow.
quote: Voles construct many surface runways and underground tunnels with numerous burrow entrances. … Most damage occurs in the winter when voles move through their grass runways under the protection of snow. … Other signs of damage by voles include 1) 1 to 2 inch-wide runways through matted grass and burrows; 2) visual sightings; 3) hawks circling overhead and diving into fields; and 4) spongy soil from burrowing activity.
source_label: CSU Extension, Managing Voles in Colorado (published May 2025, reviewed August 2025)
notes: The gopher-wire guide owns rodents; this page gives them one line and a link.

fact: One turf maker's published terms limit the maker's liability to the cost of the turf and say it will not pay for installation, labor or other incidental costs.
quote: The liability of manufacturer under this warranty shall be limited to the cost of artificial turf only. The manufacturer shall not be obligated to pay for installation, labor, or other incidental costs.
source_label: Smart Turf, published terms page (General Terms and Conditions)
notes: Page markup splits "m" and "anufacturer" across tags; the quote reads as the page renders. The warranty guide owns coverage; this page uses one line.
